experiments.question: Are booking-api@v1's schema and 35 fixtures consistent with each other and with the contract's rules, under the Ajv settings the backend's replay rig uses, and does a 365-day horizon keep the next London clock-change day bookable through the API under the real clock (Q-010 (1))?
experiments.finding: The schema compiles under Ajv2020 with strict and allErrors plus ajv-formats (as backend/test/replay.ts runs it). All 35 fixture responses validate at the top level and against their endpoint's $defs, no fixture's given bookings overlap in a room, and an independent pure model of the Interface (clock + given + request to response, with the check orders and fixed messages) reproduces every fixture exactly, a 201's id aside; all 8 error codes are exercised. By Intl, the three rooms ranges are whole local days: London 2026-11-05 (24 h), Jakarta 2026-11-05 (24 h), London 2027-10-31 (25 h). Seven negative controls are each caught. Scanning every hour from 2026-10-31 to 2031, the next London change instant is at most 217.00 days ahead (worst clock 2027-03-28T01:00Z), so 365 days covers it and 180 would not; from today it is 147 days.

routed.text: booking-api@v1 (S05) takes auth-api@v1's bearer token at all four endpoints until expiresAt and answers a missing, unknown or expired token with profile-api@v2's 401 body (G16); a restart drops tokens and keeps bookings with their ids (G17); there is no logout endpoint. The token guarantee can name booking-api@v1 with no change to auth-api's shapes or fixtures.

booking-api@v1's fixtures (hsdd/contract/fixture/booking-api/, 35, all replay exact) add two fields the current rig (backend/test/replay.ts) cannot replay: clock, the instant the injected clock reads for the whole fixture, tokens included ({{expired-token:u}} is a token whose expiresAt is before clock); and given, bookings to create before the request, directly and with the fixture's UUIDs (some lie before the clock, which POST refuses), starting each fixture from no bookings. The rig also meets DELETE, and a 204 whose fixture body is null while the real response has no body (res.json() throws on an empty body), and a 201 whose id is checked against the schema and must differ from every given id. Each fixture's response validates against the top-level schema; $defs.GetRoomsResponse, GetMyBookingsResponse, PostBookingResponse and DeleteBookingResponse are per endpoint. Booking ids are lower-case UUIDs (gen_random_uuid in PostgreSQL 17), never reused.

booking-api@v1 for the backend's plan: G6 needs a re-read after an exclusion refusal (23P01 DETAIL names one row): the room's overlapping bookings ordered by start, the first one; if none remains because it was cancelled meanwhile, try the insert again, never a 409 without error.conflict and never a 5xx from contention (G5; PRD v2 Success, 20 simultaneous attempts). G1: accept an instant only when new Date(s).toISOString() === s; query values percent-decoded. The limits are instant arithmetic: end - start <= 8 h (G9), start - now <= 8,760 h (G10), started when now >= start (G7). The title counts code points (Ajv's maxLength does, JavaScript's .length does not), needs one non-whitespace character and is stored as sent (G8). The check orders of POST and DELETE are part of the contract (G15); a DELETE id that is not a UUID answers 404. Rooms come back in PRD v2 Rooms' order with ids merapi, bromo, thames, kew; lists sort by start, ties by that order (G13, G14). produced_by is the provisional guess simple-login.backend.4 (DEC-053).

booking-api@v1 for the web's plan: web/src/test/fetchStub.ts matches String(input) against request.path, but the rooms fixtures' paths carry unencoded colons (/api/rooms?from=2026-11-05T00:00:00.000Z&to=...) while URLSearchParams writes %3A, so compare decoded URLs or build the query without encoding (the producer accepts both). A 204 fixture's body is null and new Response(body, { status: 204 }) throws on any body, so the stub answers it with no body. Fixtures carry clock and given, which explain the answer and are never sent. AC-5.3's message is written from error.conflict's roomName, start and end in the user's zone (G18); the codes to branch on are UNAUTHORIZED, VALIDATION_FAILED, BOOKING_TOO_LONG, BOOKING_STARTED, BOOKING_TOO_FAR_AHEAD, BOOKING_CONFLICT, BOOKING_NOT_FOUND (a second tab already cancelled) and BOOKING_NOT_YOURS. The form may offer end times up to start + 8 hours and dates up to 365 days ahead, but the backend's answer decides. Lists arrive sorted; no client sort is needed. consumers names simple-login.web.5 provisionally (DEC-053).

booking-api@v1 for the integration plan: the 365-day horizon keeps the next London clock-change day bookable through the API under the real clock (at most 217 days ahead from any moment, hsdd/auto/experiments/booking-api-fixtures/). PRD v2 Success's 20 simultaneous attempts must give exactly one 201 and nineteen 409 BOOKING_CONFLICT naming the winner (G5, G6); a restart keeps every booking and id but drops tokens, so the test signs in again (G17). The fixtures carry a fixed clock and seeded state that the real service under the real clock cannot reproduce: only the 14 that depend on neither (the eight 400s, the four 401s, cancel-unknown and cancel-malformed-id) can be replayed exactly through the proxy; the stateful criteria are this node's own tests. consumers names simple-login.integration.3 provisionally (DEC-053).

closes.note: Front matter governed_by: [ADR-001, ADR-002] and the body's Governed by line; every endpoint takes auth-api@v1's bearer token (Interface), and a missing, unknown or expired token is one 401 UNAUTHORIZED case with profile-api@v2's body (G16); there is no logout endpoint; bookings survive the restart that drops tokens (G17). Gate C3 reports no error for ADR-001 or ADR-002 now that the file exists.

governed_by and the Governed by line name both ADRs. Instants in toISOString form only, both directions (Values, G1); the rooms query takes the day as two instants and returns each room's bookings overlapping the half-open range, earliest first (GET /api/rooms, G13); each room carries timeZone and office (RoomWithBookings); [start, end) and touching bookings do not overlap (G3); quarter-hour instants and end after start (G2); started at the clock's reading of start or later, refused for booking and for cancelling (G7, G11); my bookings are those whose end is after the clock, soonest first (G14); the refusal carries the other booking with roomName, start and end as instants in error.conflict (Errors, G6, G18).

(1) A start at most 365 days after the backend's clock (G10, DEC-047): the experiment finds the next London change instant at most 217 days after any clock, so the next change day is always bookable through the API. (2) The refusal names the overlapping booking with the earliest start, re-read by the producer, never a 409 without one (G6, DEC-045); fixture book-overlap-several pins it.

notes: Outcome: booking-api@v1 drafted (status draft, phase_ids provisional, compatibility versioned) with four endpoints: GET /api/rooms?from&to, GET /api/me/bookings, POST /api/bookings, DELETE /api/bookings/{id} (DEC-040); one flat Booking shape everywhere (DEC-041) with UUID ids (DEC-042); eight error codes with fixed messages (DEC-043); the overlap refusal's booking in error.conflict (DEC-044), the earliest overlapping one (DEC-045); fixed check orders (DEC-048); title rule (DEC-049); strict instant form and no cap on the rooms range (DEC-050); list orders (DEC-051); fixtures with clock and given (DEC-052); provisional ids (DEC-053); what counts as breaking (DEC-054).

The two limits PRD v2 leaves to engineering, recorded with would_have_asked true for the owner's review: the longest booking is 8 hours (DEC-046, medium confidence; a statement about all-day events would move it to 12 hours or none) and a booking starts at most 365 days ahead (DEC-047, high confidence).
